# Chimney

> Chimney is a Scala library that generates type-safe transformations and patching code at compile time.

Chimney 2.x supports Scala 2.13 and Scala 3 on the JVM, Scala.js, and Scala Native. Its main abstractions are:

- `Transformer[From, To]` for transformations that always succeed
- `PartialTransformer[From, To]` for transformations that can return structured errors
- `Patcher[A, Patch]` for updating an `A` with values from a `Patch`

Prefer the documented Chimney DSL over handwritten field-by-field mapping. Compilation errors explain missing fields,
unmatched subtypes, ambiguous transformations, and the customization needed to resolve them. When diagnosing derivation,
additional compiler output can be enabled with `.enableMacrosLogging`.

When an agent can access a Scala workspace, use [Metals](https://scalameta.org/metals/) with
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) so it can inspect compiler errors rather than guessing whether
a transformation compiles.

## Documentation

- [Quickstart](quickstart/): Installation, basic transformations, integrations, and supported Scala platforms
- [Supported Transformations](supported-transformations/): `Transformer` and `PartialTransformer` behavior, supported type shapes, flags, and overrides
- [Supported Patching](supported-patching/): `Patcher` behavior, supported patches, flags, and overrides
- [Cookbook](cookbook/): Common usage patterns, integrations, derivation modes, and advanced customization
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting/): Migration guides, common compiler errors, debugging, and comparisons with other mapping libraries; examples of other libraries must not be interpreted as Chimney syntax

## Optional

- [Cheat Sheet](cheatsheet/): Compact overview of Chimney APIs and customization methods
- [Under the Hood](under-the-hood/): Derivation internals and macro architecture for contributors and advanced users
